title: kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-4
content:
Summary:
- Working notes: debugging weird mismatch in outputs when sequence length crosses certain thresholds (observed around 4096/4097 tokens). Suspect related to KV cache indexing and attention kernel selection.
- Symptoms: model outputs diverge (repeated tokens / hallucinations) only when generating with long prefixes (system + long context). Shorter contexts are OK. Deterministic repro with same seed.

Background/context:
- Model: open-arch-13B (flash-attn optimizations enabled).
- Runtime: local dev rig running serving-runtime branch 'kv-seqlen-fix-wip'.
- Config: continuous batching ON, kv_cache_shard=0, kernel_policy: auto (selects among flash_attn / flash_attn_alt / naive_attn based on seqlen/hw).

Observed repro steps (minimal):
1) Prepare prompt with ~4100 tokens prefix (random-ish sentence repeated).
2) Request generation with max_new_tokens=64, temperature=0.0, deterministic sampling.
3) Compare output to baseline (same model, but kernel_policy=force=flash_attn).

Commands tried: (from local devbox)
- curl test endpoint:
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"open-arch-13B","prompt":"<4100-token-prompt>","max_new_tokens":64,"temp":0.0}' | jq .

- python minimal repro (using runtime client):
  from runtime_client import Client
  c = Client('http://localhost:8080')
  r = c.generate(model='open-arch-13B', prompt=prefix_str, max_new_tokens=64, temperature=0.0)
  print(r.text)

- forced kernel variations:
  # force flash_attn (expected fast) -> divergence occurs
  runtime.conf.set('kernel_policy','force:flash_attn')
  # force naive_attn (expected slow) -> outputs line up with reference
  runtime.conf.set('kernel_policy','force:naive_attn')

Error snippets / logs (excerpts):
- runtime logs when divergence happens:
  [2026-02-25 14:12:03.221] WARN kernel_selector: selected flash_attn for seqlen=4097 (expected flash_attn, but output divergence)
  [2026-02-25 14:12:03.276] DEBUG kv_cache: merging kv chunks: last_index=4096 offset=0 new_chunk_len=1
  [2026-02-25 14:12:03.277] ERROR generation: inconsistent_kv_indexing detected for request_id=ab12cd34

- cuda / kernel-level complaints (rare):
  cuBLAS: invalid value (only when forcing flash_attn_alt with border cases)

What I tried and notes:
- Hypothesis A: Off-by-one in KV index when seqlen crosses a power-of-two boundary or batch-aligned chunk size (e.g., 4096). The logs show "last_index=4096 offset=0 new_chunk_len=1" which feels suspicious.
  - Experiment: instrumented kv_cache.write to assert new_chunk_start == last_index and new_chunk_len>0; assertion triggered when seqlen == 4097.

- Hypothesis B: Kernel selection logic chooses a vectorized/packed kernel for seqlen > 4096 that has a different expectation for KV layout (e.g., expects contiguous KV without chunk headers). That would explain why naive_attn (simple reference) matches but flash variants diverge.
  - Experiment: forced kernel_policy=force:naive_attn -> reproduces correct outputs but at ~3-4x latency.
  - Experiment: forced kernel_policy=force:flash_attn_alt -> sometimes crashes (cuBLAS invalid value) when seqlen around boundary.

- Hypothesis C: Padding/truncation rounding issue in batch builder: continuous batching grouping requests of different seqlens may pad to a block size, and the packed KV offsets are computed incorrectly for the padded tokens.
  - Repro note: Repro also happens when running single-request (no batching) on local devbox, so less likely purely batching issue, but runtime path still goes through 'pack_request' which does some bookkeeping.

Next debugging steps planned:
- Add per-token KV index trace for the failing request_id -> dump (index, token_id, kv_ptr) for tokens around 4090-4105.
- Add invariant checks in kernel selector: when selecting flash_attn variant, validate that computed kv_stride and offsets match expected layout; if mismatch, log detailed matrix of offsets.
- Run with ASAN on CPU fallback to catch memory-corruption (build debug binary).
- Add unit test + fuzzing for kv_cache append/merge logic around boundary cases (chunk_size values: 256, 512, 1024, 4096).

Notes on partial fixes attempted:
- Quick patch: coerce kernel selection to prefer naive_attn for seqlen >= 4097. This eliminates divergence but is not acceptable for perf.
- Another patch: change kv_cache merging to always align to 256-token boundaries by inserting dummy padding; seemed to reduce crash frequency but didn't fully fix semantics.

Trace dump example (sanitized):
- kv_index trace (token_idx : kv_ptr)
  4089 : 0x7fabc1230000
  4090 : 0x7fabc1230100
  4091 : 0x7fabc1230200
  4092 : 0x7fabc1230300
  4093 : 0x7fabc1230300  <-- duplicate ptr start (suspicious)
  4094 : 0x7fabc1230400
  4095 : 0x7fabc1230500
  4096 : 0x7fabc1230600
  4097 : 0x7fabc1230708  <-- unaligned offset (not multiple of 0x100)

This suggests write/merge didn't advance pointer size-by-token consistently for that final token.

Questions / open items:
- Is there any existing assumption in flash_attn kernels about KV packing alignment (e.g., 256-byte aligned per-token or per-row)? Need to check kernel README/docs.
- Could quantization (we're using Q4XX path for this model) impact kernel branch selection and introduce unexpected stride calculations?
- Are there known issues in upstream flash_attn variants that trigger at seqlen > 4096? Search GH issues (todo).

Immediate mitigation for prod: add a rollout flag to routing policy that forces 'compat' kernel for seqlen>threshold and allow per-customer override. But need to estimate perf cost.

Logs / artifacts to attach to ticket: request_id ab12cd34 full debug dump (saved locally: /tmp/ab12cd34-debug.tar.gz), kernel selector metrics (metrics/kernel_selector/2026-02-25.csv), kv_cache trace (/tmp/kv-trace-4097.log).

Potential long-term fixes:
- Make kernel selector emit a compatibility check and fallback automatically when offsets don't match expected layout.
- Unify KV packing layout across kernels (define a strict ABI).
- Add integration test in CI that runs generation with edge seqlens (4095-4105) for each kernel variant (flash_attn, flash_attn_alt, naive_attn).

Misc notes:
- I suspect the root cause is a small arithmetic rounding bug in the KV merge path when handling the very last token appended to a chunk; this interacts poorly with a 'fast path' in flash_attn that assumes contiguous tightly-packed KV without extra header bytes.
- If confirmed, fix should be simple (normalize chunk sizes and ensure pointer increments are token_stride-aligned), but need to be careful to preserve memory layout for existing stored snapshots (back-compat).

Next immediate TODOs (priority):
- [ ] Add KV per-token trace and reproduce locally with debug build (ASAN).
- [ ] Add kernel_selector invariant checks and more verbose logging (only when debug enabled).
- [ ] Create CI matrix job for seqlen edge cases across kernels.
- [ ] Open GH issue linking this repro + attach minimal repro script.

If anyone else is digging into this, ping me in #kernels-debug channel. I'll drop the debug tar to the ticket and link.

-- Arjun
  (notes are messy, will clean up after first round of triage)
